sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house in Federal Way?
sections.html:
Most Federal Way owners choose among a listing with an agent, a sale they run themselves, and a direct purchase by a buyer who pays without a mortgage. The right one depends on the condition of the house, how soon you need to move, and what you still owe on it.

  • Agent listing: You prepare the house, allow showings and negotiate whatever repairs the buyer's inspection turns up. It reaches the widest pool of buyers and asks the most patience.
  • Selling it yourself: You set the price, market the house and handle the paperwork, including the seller disclosure statement that Washington requires for improved residential property unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt.
  • Direct cash purchase: The buyer is not waiting on a lender, so the sale does not hinge on loan approval. Compare the written offer with what you would net after the loan payoff, taxes and any repairs you would otherwise pay for.

sections.h2: What is Federal Way like, and why does it matter for a sale?
sections.html:
Federal Way sits in the southwest corner of King County, about 25 miles south of Seattle. The city covers 23.72 square miles, 22.32 of them land, and it holds lakes such as Steel Lake and Lake Killarney. Its name came from a school district formed in 1929, which in turn took the name of U.S. Route 99, today's Pacific Highway South.

The city is young on paper. Voters turned down incorporation in 1971, 1981 and 1985 before approving it on February 28, 1990. Interstate 5 opened through the area in October 1962 and turned it into a commuter community for Seattle workers. Weyerhaeuser opened its headquarters complex east of I-5 in 1971 and announced in 2014 that it would leave, and World Vision's U.S. headquarters is also here.

Wikipedia describes the city as marked by 1990s semi-urban development: landscaped apartment complexes and shopping centers, with The Commons at Federal Way as the only indoor mall, at South 320th Street and SR 99. Parks give some neighborhoods their pull. Steel Lake Park sits on South 312th Street, Dash Point State Park is the only developed waterfront park inside the city, and West Hylebos Wetlands Park holds the Barker Cabin, built in 1883 and the oldest known building in Federal Way.

Summers are warm and dry, and no monthly average temperature tops 71.6 degrees Fahrenheit. A few neighborhoods to the east, including Star Lake, Camelot, Lakeland and Jovita, were named potential annexation areas, and residents of the East Federal Way area rejected annexation by 66 to 34 percent on August 21, 2007. Confirm that your parcel is inside city limits before you contact the Permit Center.

sections.h2: How much excise tax will I owe when I sell in Federal Way?
sections.html:
The seller owes it. Washington's real estate excise tax is the seller's obligation under RCW 82.45.080, and the Department of Revenue says it is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, whether or not the deed is recorded that day. A deeded sale of a Federal Way house is reported to King County, where the city lies.

The state portion is graduated. Under the thresholds now posted by the Department of Revenue, the first $525,000 of the price is taxed at 1.1 percent, the slice up to $1,525,000 at 1.28 percent, the slice up to $3,025,000 at 2.75 percent, and anything above that at 3 percent. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the cut points move to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. A local rate is added on top, so ask your escrow officer for the figure that applies to your parcel.

As an example, a sale at the $552,800 median value would carry about $6,131 in state tax: $5,775 on the first $525,000 and about $356 on the rest. The tax must be paid within one month of the sale, or penalty and interest begin, and unpaid tax can become a lien on the property. Ask for the excise tax to appear as its own line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Do I need a permit or approval before selling a Federal Way house?
sections.html:
The City of Federal Way Permit Center handles building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, demolition and fire prevention permits, along with land use and sign permits. It is the office to ask about repairs you plan to finish before a sale, or about work a previous owner may have done without a permit.

  • Phone and email: 253-835-2607 or permitcenter@federalwaywa.gov.
  • Hours: 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. The center is closed to the public on Wednesdays and on city holidays, including the day after Thanksgiving.
  • Applications: Anything that needs review is submitted electronically after you request a Document Upload Link, which can take a few days. Residential electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits can be applied for online through My Building Permit.

The city also warns that it will not unexpectedly ask for payment by wire transfer based on an email. If a message claims to be from the city and asks for money, call the Permit Center before you send anything. For parcel numbers, use the city's maps, the King County Parcel Viewer, or ask the Permit Center.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and schools shape buyer interest in Federal Way?
sections.html:
Federal Way is served by Interstate 5 at the 348th Street, 320th Street and 272nd Street exits and by State Route 99, the Pacific Highway. The Federal Way Transit Center on 23rd Avenue South is served by King County Metro, Pierce Transit and Sound Transit Express, and the Link light rail extension to Federal Way Downtown station opened in December 2025. Average travel time to work is 32.1 minutes, so access to the freeway and the station is a real selling point for commuters.

Public schools come from Federal Way Public Schools, the district that formed in 1929 as School District No. 210. When you describe your house to a buyer, name the nearest park, the nearest I-5 exit and the walk or drive to the station.

sections.h2: What should I check before I accept an offer on my Federal Way house?
sections.html:
• Get the offer in writing, with the price, the closing date and who pays each closing cost.
  • Request a payoff statement from your lender so you know the exact balance.
  • Ask the buyer for proof of funds, and ask whether the offer depends on repairs or an inspection.
  • Estimate your excise tax with the rates above and ask escrow for the local rate.
  • Find out whether the buyer expects the house to be emptied, and by what date.
  • Compare the net figure from each route, not the headline price alone.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax on a house sale in Federal Way?
faqs.a: The seller. RCW 82.45.080 makes the tax the seller's obligation, and the Department of Revenue notes that if the seller does not pay, the buyer becomes responsible. Unpaid tax can create a lien on the property.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Federal Way house?
faqs.a: First-half taxes are due by April 30 and second-half taxes by October 31. RCW 84.56.020 makes the county treasurer the collector, so Federal Way owners pay through King County. Ask the county for the current statement on your parcel.

faqs.q: Which county is Federal Way in?
faqs.a: King County. The city lies in the southwest corner of the county, about 25 miles south of Seattle, so deeds, excise tax affidavits and property tax bills for a Federal Way home go through King County offices.

faqs.q: How do I find my parcel number in Federal Way?
faqs.a: Use the City's maps or the King County Parcel Viewer, or contact the Permit Center at 253-835-2607 or permitcenter@federalwaywa.gov. You will need the parcel number for permit questions and for title work.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a seller disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Usually yes. RCW 64.06.020 requires the seller of improved residential property to deliver a completed disclosure statement within five business days after a written contract is accepted, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind.
